message.reasoning:
Ready to play Monopoly.

I now own MEDITERRANEAN_AVENUE, VENTNOR_AVENUE, and PENNSYLVANIA_AVENUE after a trade with p4. I no longer hold MARVIN_GARDENS or READING_RAILROAD. The yellow monopoly requires three properties, so I still need Atlantic Avenue.

Pennsylvania Avenue is green, not yellow. I do not have a yellow monopoly.

I cannot build houses. p1 owns Vermont, St. Charles, States, St. James, and Water Works. They have no monopoly.

p3 owns a dark blue monopoly with one house on each property. They have $222 cash, enough to build one more house on either space and leave $22 remaining.

p4 has $1,492 cash and owns Reading Railroad, Oriental, Connecticut, Electric Company, Pennsylvania Railroad, and Marvin Gardens. They received $350 from the trade.

I have no monopolies. I hold one of three brown properties, one of three yellow properties, and one of three green properties.

I cannot build houses. I am weighing three paths to a monopoly. The yellow set is blocked because I traded away Marvin Gardens. The brown set would require landing on Baltic Avenue, which is unowned, but I should not trade Mediterranean away yet. The green set needs Pacific and North Carolina, both also unowned.

I will not mortgage. I have enough cash and would lose rent income.

I am considering trading with p1 or p4 to complete a set. p1 holds Water Works and St. James. p4 has two railroads and lots of cash. I do not want to trade away my only brown property for Marvin Gardens.

I cannot trade with p4 to complete a set. Their light blue set requires Vermont from p1, not from me. I cannot trade with p1 either. They do not hold properties that would complete my monopolies.

I will not trade with p3. They need cash to build more houses on their dark blue set, and that would raise rent for everyone including me.

p4 has $1,492 and wants a light blue monopoly, but p1 refused to sell Vermont. I am considering whether p4 might be willing to trade Marvin Gardens for my Ventnor Avenue.

The trade that gave away Marvin Gardens and Reading Railroad for Ventnor and Pennsylvania Avenue was a clear mistake. I will not repeat it.

I considered trading for p4's Oriental and Connecticut to complete a light blue monopoly. That set is their only remaining path to a monopoly, so they will not sell it cheaply.

I am now calculating a price for p4's Oriental and Connecticut pair. A light blue monopoly is worth roughly $400 to $600, and I have $901. I would pay about $500 plus another property to acquire the set.

I am now considering offering $600 cash for p4's Oriental and Connecticut pair. That would give me a light blue monopoly, leave me with $301 in cash, and allow me to build two houses on each property.

I realized that two houses on each light blue property would leave me with only one dollar after paying $600. That is too little to survive a Boardwalk rent of $600 from p3. I am now considering paying about $400 instead.

I am now calculating the exact survival math for p3's Boardwalk. Paying $400 for the light blue pair leaves me with $501 after building two houses on each property, which is barely enough to cover a one-house Boardwalk rent of $200. I also considered paying $250 to build three houses, but that would leave only $201 and still be too risky against p3's dark blue set.

I need to keep roughly $600 in cash to survive a two-house Boardwalk rent. Any trade that spends more than about $300 would leave me too exposed.

I will end my turn. I will not trade or mortgage. I will keep my $901 cash to survive a two-house Boardwalk rent. I am hoping to land on Baltic Avenue, Virginia, or other unowned properties.

I considered trading my three scattered properties for p4's Oriental and Connecticut pair to complete a light blue monopoly without spending cash. I rejected this offer because p4 would not want three scattered properties in exchange for their two-of-three light blue set.
